answer: A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, which means it pays the knoll fee twice and still divides one payout. Because the relic ledger attributes every share, the horizon audit makes public the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 69% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. That is 8 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
